note.headline: Chips sold, defensives bought, S&P 500 falls while Dow and Russell hold
note.standfirst: The S&P 500 fell 0.50% as semiconductors gave back the week's gains, while the Dow and Russell 2000 closed higher on a rotation into health care and staples. Breadth stayed roughly balanced at 1.36 advancers to decliners, so this was a sector trade, not a broad risk-off move.
takeaways: Nasdaq 100 fell 1.99% on a semiconductor unwind, led by AMD down 8.86% and Nvidia down 5.86%.
The Dow rose 0.85% and the Russell 2000 rose 0.57% as health care and staples absorbed the rotation out of tech.
The curve flattened, with 5s30s down 5bp and 3m10y down 5bp, while the dollar index fell 0.48% to a fresh high on the YTD measure.
Gold, silver, platinum, palladium, and copper all fell together, with copper the single largest drag on the risk barometer at -1.89.
note.desk_view:
The session confirms a rotation, not a risk event. Technology gave up 3.26% on the sector and the Nasdaq 100 underperformed the S&P 500, but the Russell 2000 and the Dow both closed in the green and breadth held near even. Credit did not confirm the equity weakness: high yield fell 0.12% and investment grade fell 0.14%, nowhere near the kind of spread widening that would mark a genuine risk-off session. VIX actually fell 0.98% into the close. If this were a broad deleveraging, small caps and credit would have led the damage. They did not.

The level that decides whether this persists is the Nasdaq 100 relative to the S&P 500. A second session of chip-led underperformance without broader index damage would confirm a pure positioning unwind in the most crowded trade of the year. A break where the Russell and Dow roll over too would say something else is going on, and the commodity complex gives a reason to watch closely: copper, silver, platinum, and palladium all fell together, and copper was the largest single drag on the risk barometer. That is a growth signal, not a tech-specific one, and it sits uneasily next to the equity rotation. Watch whether industrial metals keep leading or whether this was a one-day flush.
watching: Whether semiconductor weakness extends into a second session or stays contained to AMD, Nvidia, and Broadcom.
Copper and industrial metals follow-through, given the -1.89 contribution to the risk barometer.
The dollar index at a fresh multi-horizon high after a down day, and whether EUR/USD and GBP/USD lows hold.
Credit spreads on HYG and LQD for confirmation or denial of the equity rotation story.
note.equities:
The S&P 500 closed down 0.50% at 7201.09, with the index-level move entirely a function of the Nasdaq 100's 1.99% decline. The Dow added 0.85% to 50018.70 and the Russell 2000 rose 0.57%, so large-cap value and small caps both outperformed the mega-cap growth complex by a wide margin on the day. Breadth was 15 advancers to 11 decliners, a ratio of 1.36, which does not support a broad selloff narrative. Dispersion printed 2.97.

Sector rotation was the story. Health care led at +2.95% on XLV, with Pfizer up 3.87% and Eli Lilly up 3.15%. Consumer staples rose 1.66%, real estate rose 1.31%, and financials rose 0.83%. Technology was the outlier at -3.26%, dragged by AMD down 8.86%, Nvidia down 5.86%, Broadcom down 3.98%, and Oracle down 3.68%. Industrials slipped 0.53%. The pattern is a clean swap out of semiconductors and into health care and staples, not a market-wide repricing.
note.rates:
The curve flattened. 5s30s came in 5bp to 55bp and 3m10y came in 5bp to 55bp, while 2s10s held unchanged at 29bp. The 10-year sits at 4.92% and the 30-year at 5.29%, both level readings from the prior session's close given the holiday-adjusted publication schedule. The 2-year held at 4.63%.

The move is consistent with a long-end bid against a stable front end, which fits a day where equity money rotated toward defensives rather than fled risk outright. Breakevens were mixed and small: the 5-year breakeven fell 4bp to 2.11% and sits at a fresh low, the 10-year breakeven fell 1bp to 2.12%, while the 5y5y forward ticked up 2bp to 2.13%. MOVE fell 2.05% to 98.838, suggesting rate vol eased even as the curve shape shifted.
note.credit: Credit held steady and did not confirm the equity rotation. High yield (HYG) fell 0.12% to a fresh low on the YTD measure, investment grade (LQD) fell 0.14%, and EM sovereign debt (EMB) fell 0.34%, the largest single drag on the risk barometer among credit instruments at -0.93. Leveraged loans slipped 0.10%. None of these moves are large enough to call spread widening. The tone is soft but orderly, a market pricing modest caution rather than stress.
note.fx: The dollar index fell 0.48% to 103.825 even as it sits at a fresh high across the 1-month, 3-month, and 6-month windows, a reminder that the broader uptrend is intact despite the day's pullback. EUR/USD fell 0.03% to a fresh low at 1.097, while GBP/USD rose 0.13% to 1.311. USD/JPY rose 0.18% to 159.223. In EM, USD/MXN rose 1.84% to a fresh high at 19.427, USD/TRY rose 0.17% to a fresh high at 50.662, and USD/CNY fell 0.20%. The EM currency complex is split, with Mexico and Turkey under the most visible pressure.
note.commodities: Energy diverged from metals. WTI rose 1.85% to 81.65 while Brent fell 0.97% to 88.50, and natural gas jumped 15.33%. Precious and industrial metals sold off together: gold fell 2.65%, silver fell 5.65% to a fresh low, platinum fell 4.94% to a fresh low, palladium fell 4.16% to a fresh low, and copper fell 2.53%, the largest single drag on the day's risk barometer. Aluminium fell 5.00%. In ags, corn rose 3.69%, cocoa rose 4.98%, and coffee fell 5.09%.
note.volatility: VIX fell 0.98% to 26.36 and VIX9D fell 3.89% to 26.68, both easing into the close even as the cash index sold off, a sign the rotation was not read as a volatility event. VIX3M fell slightly to 25.47, keeping the curve in a mild backwardation given VIX9D above VIX3M. VVIX fell 2.80% to 114.07. SKEW, last published the prior session, sat at 140.37. The cost of near-dated protection eased on a down day for the Nasdaq, consistent with a rotation story rather than a demand for broad portfolio insurance.
note.digital: Bitcoin fell 2.20% to 59862.90, broadly in line with the session's risk-off tilt in growth assets, while Ether fell 1.66% and Solana fell 3.45%. XRP fell 1.84%. Bitcoin's -1.07 contribution to the risk barometer was the second-largest drag after copper, and the move tracked the Nasdaq's underperformance closely enough to suggest digital assets traded as a high-beta extension of the tech unwind rather than on any idiosyncratic catalyst.
note.international: European indices closed broadly lower ahead of the US open, with the EURO STOXX 50 down 1.16%, the DAX down 1.26%, and the FTSE MIB down 1.84%, while the CAC and FTSE 100 were closer to flat. Asia was split: the Nikkei surged 3.91% and the KOSPI jumped 6.32%, with TAIEX up 8.99%, while the Hang Seng fell 0.73% to a fresh low. The handoff to New York was mixed at best, with European tech-adjacent weakness pre-figuring the Nasdaq's decline, while the strength in Japan, Korea, and Taiwan did not carry through to US chip names.
note.correlation:
The session's defining feature was a correlation breakdown between equities and credit. Equities fell on a tech-specific rotation while credit spreads barely moved, a divergence that would not survive a genuine risk-off episode. At the same time, bitcoin and the Nasdaq moved together, and copper, silver, platinum, and palladium all fell in the same session, which argues for a growth-sensitive thread running under the commodity complex that the equity rotation alone does not explain.

A break in the current pattern, where credit starts pricing the same caution equities did today, would change the read entirely. Watch HYG and LQD into the next session: if spreads widen alongside continued chip weakness, the rotation story gives way to a broader deleveraging narrative, and the Russell's resilience today would likely not hold.
